questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Ratio form of 2/3 is
questions.explanation: The fraction a/b is written as the ratio a:b.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: A rational number with no reciprocal is
questions.explanation: The reciprocal of 0 would be 1/0, which is undefined.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Distance of circular path of a circle is
questions.answer: circumference
questions.explanation: The distance around a circle is its circumference.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: In 5^2, the power is
questions.explanation: In a^n, a is the base and n is the power (exponent).

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The order of rotational symmetry of a square is ____________.
questions.explanation: A square maps onto itself 4 times in a full turn (at 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°).

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: An example for a sphere is ____________.
questions.answer: A ball (football / globe)

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Use a suitable sign (>, <, =) in the blank: 1/(-11) ____________ (-1)/11
questions.review: Fraction layout was lost in the PDF text; read as 1/(-11) ___ (-1)/11. Check against the PDF.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The name of the line drawn perpendicular to its base in a parallelogram is ____________.
questions.answer: Height (altitude)

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Write the coefficient of x in the expression ab + 3ax.
questions.answer: 3a
questions.explanation: In the term 3ax, the factor that multiplies x is 3a.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Which is the base number in 6^1?

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: What is the order of rotational symmetry of the letter 'C'?
questions.explanation: 'C' looks the same only after a full 360° turn.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Mention the total number of faces in a cuboid.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Identify and write the like terms among the following terms: 5n, 8a, 9a, 3n, 19n
questions.answer: Like terms: 5n, 3n, 19n (all contain n) and 8a, 9a (both contain a).

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: List out the English alphabets which have linear symmetry.
questions.answer: A, B, C, D, E, H, I, K, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y
questions.explanation: Each can be folded along a vertical or horizontal line so the two halves match.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Calculate the value of: 20% of 10 litre.
questions.answer: 2 litre

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Find the simplest form of: 128/(-64)
questions.explanation: Divide numerator and denominator by 64: 2/(-1) = -2.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Construct a factor tree for 12x²y².
questions.answer: 12x²y² = 12 × x² × y²; 12 = 2 × 2 × 3, x² = x × x, y² = y × y. So 12x²y² = 2 × 2 × 3 × x × x × y × y.
questions.review: Factor-tree drawing; the key gives the final factorisation only.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Simplify: 6^0 × 4^3
questions.explanation: 6^0 = 1 and 4^3 = 64, so the product is 1 × 64 = 64.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Draw any two figures which do not have linear symmetry.
questions.answer: Any two, e.g. a scalene triangle and a (non-rectangular) parallelogram; letters such as F, G, J, L, N, P, Q, R, S, Z also have no line of symmetry.
questions.review: Drawing question; answer is guidance for the marker.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Write the names of the following solids: (i) a rectangular box, (ii) a pyramid with a triangular base, (iii) a cone, (iv) a square box (figures shown in the paper).
questions.answer: (i) Cuboid, (ii) Triangular pyramid, (iii) Cone, (iv) Cube
questions.review: Question depends on a picture. Names are read from the PDF image; confirm them and consider attaching a figure.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: In a class of 50 students, if 2/5 of them are girls, find the number of boys present in the class.
questions.answer: 30 boys

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Copy the given figure (a 5 × 5 grid with some shaded squares), construct any one diagonal in it, and shade some more regions to make it a symmetrical figure.
questions.answer: Draw the grid, draw one diagonal as the line of symmetry, and shade the mirror image of each shaded square on the other side of the diagonal.
questions.review: Drawing question with a figure; answer is guidance for the marker.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: For a certain amount, the interest at 5% rate for a time period of 3 years is ₹450. Find the amount.
questions.review: Paper marks this 4. Stored as 5 only if --four-mark-as 5 is used.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Draw a circle of radius 5 cm and mark the centre 'O', radius 'OA' and diameter 'AB'.
questions.answer: Mark O; with the compass set to 5 cm draw the circle; mark A on the circle and join OA (5 cm); extend AO to meet the circle at B so that AB = 10 cm passes through O.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The rate that represents pulse is,
questions.answer: Pulse rate
questions.explanation: Pulse rate is the number of heartbeats felt per minute.
questions.review: Question wording is ambiguous (pulse rate vs heartbeat). Confirm the intended answer.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An object moving in a circular path starts from point A and returns to point A. The distance travelled is:
questions.answer: 2πr
questions.explanation: The distance for one full round is the circumference, 2πr.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In the electric circuit diagram shown (battery, bulb, wires and a safety-pin arrangement), which object is used as a switch?
questions.answer: Safety pin
questions.explanation: Pressing the safety pin onto the pin/drawing pin closes the circuit, so it acts as the switch.
questions.review: Depends on a circuit diagram; answer read from the picture.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The lens used in microscopes is:
questions.answer: Convex lens
questions.explanation: A convex lens magnifies small objects.
questions.review: Biconvex is also a convex lens; confirm which option the textbook expects.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In plant reproduction, seeds are dispersed by birds and wind through ____________.
questions.answer: seed dispersal (agents such as animals and wind)
questions.review: Blank is loosely worded; confirm the expected word.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The SI unit of time is ____________.
questions.answer: second

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: If the electric current is high, the fuse wire ____________.
questions.answer: melts
questions.explanation: The heat of a large current melts the fuse wire and breaks the circuit.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Forests prevent ____________ erosion.
questions.answer: soil

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is the male reproductive part of a flower?
questions.answer: Stamen

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is a source of light?
questions.answer: An object that gives out its own light, e.g. the Sun.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What happens if we throw waste into water bodies?
questions.answer: The water gets polluted, harming aquatic life and making the water unsafe to use.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: On which day is World Water Day celebrated?
questions.answer: 22 March

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: List the differences between arteries and veins.
questions.answer: Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood away from the heart (except the pulmonary artery); they have thick, elastic walls and no valves. Veins carry blood back to the heart (oxygen-poor, except the pulmonary vein); they have thinner walls and valves.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What are the parts included in the human excretory system?
questions.answer: Two kidneys, two ureters, the urinary bladder and the urethra.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Uniform motion is called effortless motion. Why?
questions.answer: In uniform motion the speed and direction stay constant, so no extra force or effort is needed to change the motion once it has started.
questions.review: Textbook reasoning may differ; check wording.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A bicycle travels 5 km in 20 minutes. What is its average speed?
questions.answer: 15 km/h

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Why is nichrome wire used in electric stoves?
questions.answer: Nichrome has high resistance and a high melting point, so it gets very hot without melting and does not oxidise easily.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: List two devices that work based on the heating effect of electric current.
questions.answer: Electric heater and electric iron (also toaster, geyser, electric kettle).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: What is the use of a plane mirror?
questions.answer: A plane mirror is used to see our own image (e.g. dressing mirrors) and in devices like periscopes and kaleidoscopes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The image seen in a stainless steel plate is erect and of the same size as the object. Why?
questions.answer: A polished steel plate acts like a plane mirror and reflects light regularly, so the image is erect and the same size as the object.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: As a responsible person, how can we reduce sewage waste?
questions.answer: Use water carefully, do not throw solid waste, oil or chemicals into drains, and reuse or treat waste water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: How can the impurities in sewage water be classified?
questions.answer: Impurities in sewage are classified as suspended, dissolved and biological (microbial) impurities; they can also be grouped as organic and inorganic.
questions.review: Classification scheme differs between sources; check against the textbook.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Explain the role of forests in maintaining ecological balance.
questions.answer: Forests keep the oxygen–carbon dioxide balance, help rainfall, prevent soil erosion, conserve groundwater and give food and shelter to wildlife.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Draw a labeled diagram showing fertilization in plants.
questions.answer: Diagram of a carpel: stigma, style, ovary, ovule, pollen tube carrying male gametes to the egg cell, with the zygote formed in the ovule.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: First War of Indian Independence (1857 – 58 C.E)
questions.text: He regarded the 1857 revolt as India's First War of Independence.
questions.answer: V.D. Savarkar
questions.explanation: V.D. Savarkar's book described the 1857 revolt as the First War of Indian Independence.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Unification of Karnataka and Border Disputes
questions.text: In this literary work it is mentioned that Karnataka extends from the Kaveri to the Godavari.
questions.answer: Kavirajamarga
questions.explanation: Kavirajamarga (c. 9th century) describes the Kannada land between the Kaveri and the Godavari.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: In this year the Atmiya Sabha (Friendly Society) was established.
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha in Calcutta in 1814.
questions.review: Some sources give 1815; 1814 is the only listed option near it. Confirm with the textbook.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: It is about twice the size of India and is the 7th continent of the world. (A map of the continent is shown in the paper.)
questions.answer: Australia
questions.explanation: Australia is the smallest continent and about twice the size of India.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Who gave the slogan "If you give me blood, I will give you freedom"?
questions.answer: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Whom did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar consider his philosophical guide?
questions.answer: Gautama Buddha
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess; Ambedkar also named Kabir and Jyotiba Phule as gurus.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What is the Chipko Movement?
questions.answer: A movement in which villagers hugged trees to stop them being cut down.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What are natural resources?
questions.answer: Resources that nature provides, such as water, soil, forests, minerals and air.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: The total number of member states of the United Nations is ____________.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: 'Black Wood' in the continent of Australia is ____________.
questions.answer: Acacia (Australian blackwood)

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: The defence portfolios of our nation are given to the ____________.
questions.answer: Ministry of Defence (headed by the Defence Minister)

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: ____________ continent is reserved only for scientific research.
questions.answer: Antarctica

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What were the major movements led by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar against untouchability and social discrimination?
questions.answer: The Mahad Satyagraha (1927) for the right to use public water, the Kalaram temple-entry movement (1930), and the founding of the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha to uplift the depressed classes.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Unification of Karnataka and Border Disputes
questions.text: Name the organizations that contributed to the unification of Karnataka.
questions.answer: Karnataka Vidyavardhaka Sangha, Karnataka Sahitya Parishat, Karnataka Sabha and the Karnataka Ekikarana Sabha.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Name the major environmental movements.
questions.answer: Chipko Movement, Appiko Movement, Silent Valley Movement and Narmada Bachao Andolan.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What were the benefits of land reform measures?
questions.answer: Tenants became owners of the land they tilled, landlord exploitation reduced, land ceilings spread land more fairly, and farm output and rural incomes rose.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Analyze the role of mass media in the development of a country.
questions.answer: Mass media spread information and awareness, educate people, shape public opinion, keep governments accountable and support trade and culture.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Why do we need courts?
questions.answer: Courts settle disputes, punish wrongdoers, protect fundamental rights and make sure laws and the Constitution are followed.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What are the responsibilities of the defence forces?
questions.answer: They protect the country from external attack, guard its borders, help in disasters and keep peace.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: State (list) the neighbouring countries of India.
questions.answer: Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar; Sri Lanka and the Maldives are island neighbours.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Name the important heads of state who played a prominent role in the establishment of the United Nations.
questions.answer: Franklin D. Roosevelt (USA), Winston Churchill (UK) and Joseph Stalin (USSR).

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: List the Indian research centres in Antarctica.
questions.answer: Dakshin Gangotri, Maitri and Bharati.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Analyze the role of the Brahma Samaj in eliminating social evils in India.
questions.answer: Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828, it opposed sati, idol worship and caste discrimination, supported widow remarriage and women's education, and promoted a rational, one-God religion.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: First War of Indian Independence (1857 – 58 C.E)
questions.text: Draw the map of India and mark the following: Delhi, Gwalior, Allahabad, Kanpur.
questions.answer: Outline map of India with the four 1857 centres marked at their correct positions and labelled.
